svg.text: Where each part runs, what it does, and how far along it is. Your local files stay on your device. The firm cloud holds only text copied from sources the firm connects.
Ask, search, Sources and Connectors screens. Shows which passages
are local and which are cloud.
Asks the firm cloud for matching passages, merges them with local
Encrypted database of your local files' text. Never uploaded
Reads PDFs, Word, Excel and scans on this device. Scans use the
Stay where they are. The app only reads the folders you approve.
Holds the index encryption key and the sign-in tokens (Keychain
Sends your question and the chosen passages straight to Bedrock.
Uses your own AWS login for now.
Search, connectors list, connect, sync, disconnect. Checks every request's sign-in and firm.
Synced text, file names and who may read each file. Firms are kept apart by row-level security
inside the database. Planned on RDS.
Reads PDF, Word, Excel and PowerPoint
files. Empty environment, time and memory
Pulls files and permissions from Google and
Microsoft every few minutes. Resumes after
Required two-step sign-in. The firm ID is
set by us and users cannot change it.
Holds each firm's long-lived Google and
Microsoft access. Developer machines use a
One key for the platform, one for audit
logs, one per firm for files and secrets.
Created but not used yet. Original files
CloudTrail records every file access, GuardDuty watches for threats, alerts go to email.
Will give each app short-lived permission to call Claude directly, so firms need no AWS login
access. Passwords go only to them.
Read-only access to files and sharing
Answers questions. Zero data retention must
be on before anything is sent.
Your question text goes to the firm cloud to be searched. Matching passages come
back. Nothing from your local files goes up.
Sign-in to the firm's account. The firm and your role come from the sign-in
The question and the best passages (local and cloud) go straight to Claude on
Bedrock. The firm cloud never sees this step.
An administrator approves access at Google or Microsoft. A one-time code comes
back to the API, which swaps it for the long-lived token.
The API reads and writes synced text and permissions. Every query is limited to
one firm by the database itself.
The worker stores passages, names and permissions. It never stores the original
Each downloaded file is handed to a locked-down reader process and discarded;
The worker fetches the firm's access token to read from Google and Microsoft.
Read-only file listing, sharing settings and downloads from the connected
When a source is connected, the API saves its long-lived token in the secret
store. The database never holds a token.
Status as of 2 November 2026. Nothing is deployed to AWS yet; the cloud side runs on a developer machine for testing.
